models.author: Freimut Diener
models.description:
# SSD MobileNet V2 FPNLite 320x320 (COCO17)

## Overview

This dataset contains the pretrained **SSD MobileNet V2 FPNLite 320x320** object detection model from the TensorFlow 2 Object Detection Model Zoo.

Model name:
`ssd_mobilenet_v2_fpnlite_320x320_coco17_tpu-8`

The model is trained on the **COCO 2017** dataset and designed for lightweight, fast, and real-time object detection tasks.

---

## Features

- TensorFlow 2 compatible
- Lightweight SSD MobileNet V2 architecture
- FPNLite backbone for improved detection performance
- Trained on COCO17
- Optimized for TPU-8
- Fast inference for edge and mobile applications

---

## Architecture

- **Framework:** TensorFlow 2
- **Model Type:** SSD (Single Shot Detector)
- **Backbone:** MobileNet V2 + FPNLite
- **Input Resolution:** 320×320
- **Dataset:** COCO 2017

---

## Contents

This dataset includes files extracted from:

`ssd_mobilenet_v2_fpnlite_320x320_coco17_tpu-8.tar.gz`

Typical contents:
- SavedModel
- Checkpoints
- Pipeline configuration
- Label mappings
- Training metadata

---

## Use Cases

- Real-time object detection
- Edge AI deployment
- TensorFlow Object Detection API projects
- Transfer learning
- Computer vision research
- Educational deep learning experiments

---

## Source

Official TensorFlow Model Zoo release:
http://download.tensorflow.org/models/object_detection/tf2/20200711/ssd_mobilenet_v2_fpnlite_320x320_coco17_tpu-8.tar.gz

---

## License

Please refer to the original TensorFlow Model Zoo license and usage terms.

Model Summary

BEATs (Bidirectional Encoder representation from Audio Transformers) is a transformer-based self-supervised audio representation model developed by Microsoft Research for general-purpose audio understanding.

The model learns semantic audio representations from large-scale unlabeled audio data and can be fine-tuned for downstream tasks such as:

-> Audio classification
->Bioacoustic analysis
->Bird sound detection
-> Acoustic event recognition

This project uses pretrained BEATs checkpoints released by Microsoft Research. Special acknowledgments to the BEATs authors and Microsoft Research for making the pretrained models publicly available and supporting open research in audio representation learning.
